correctness.rationale: For q>=2 and 0<r<1, the subcritical resolvent kernel equals (1-r²)/(1-rA+qr²) on the full adjacency spectrum [-2sqrt(q),2sqrt(q)]. Differentiating r yields g_r(t) strictly increasing, so its endpoint constraints give exactly the two sharp b bounds. At r=q^{-1/2}, the Vergara radial positivity matrix becomes r^{i+j}(min(i,j)+1)(alpha+beta max(i,j)), with PSD precisely between b=0 and b=(q-1)/(q+1): negativity of diagonals for b<0, of 2x2 minors for larger b; endpoint Gram matrices and convexity show sufficiency. For r above critical, normalized adjacent-index minors tend to -[beta/(1-(qr²)^-1)]², excluding b!=0, and pure r^distance is PSD via negative-type tree metric. This proves all finite subsets and included boundaries analytically; the independent SymPy and Fraction checks only corroborate formulas and one minor.
